# 'Rails Have Shifted'—Stablecoins Topped ACH At $7.5 Trillion A Month

By [Boaz Sobrado](https://www.forbes.com/sites/boazsobrado/ "https://www.forbes.com/sites/boazsobrado/"),

Former Contributor.

Forbes contributors publish independent expert analyses and insights.
Boaz Sobrado is a fintech leader and entrepreneur.

Apr 20, 2026, 09:15am EDT

0

"In February alone, stablecoin monthly volume hit $7.2 trillion, surpassing the US ACH network ($6.8T) for the first time in history," wrote Haonan Li, the co-founder and CEO of stablecoin payments firm Codex and a former Optimism core contributor.

The post landed in mid-April. American payments executives took a few weeks to notice.

The numbers come from [Artemis Analytics](https://app.artemisanalytics.com/stablecoins). Stablecoin onchain settlement hit $7.2 trillion in February on a 30-day rolling basis. The US Automated Clearing House, the rail that has carried American payroll and B2B payments for half a century, settled $6.8 trillion in the same window. March brought $7.5 trillion in onchain stablecoin volume. The crossover is no longer a one-off.

OKX, the verified crypto exchange, put it bluntly two days after Haonan. "The payment rails have shifted. $7.2T in monthly stablecoin volume proves it," the exchange wrote on April 16.

For Visa, Mastercard and the US banks that built ACH, the comfortable story is over. Stablecoins are not a crypto-trader curiosity. They are a payment rail.

PROMOTED

## USDC Has Quietly Overtaken USDT

The other shift inside the headline number is the dollar doing the work.

Circle's USDC processed roughly $2.2 trillion in adjusted year-to-date onchain volume. Tether's USDT did $1.3 trillion. The figures come from [Mizuho Securities research](https://whale-alert.io/stories/f79601790098db/USDC-overtook-USDT-in-adjusted-YTD-on-chain-volume-22T-vs-13T-says-Mizuho) shared in April. USDC now leads adjusted volume for the first time since 2019. Tether still dominates total market cap at around $184 billion versus USDC at $75-80 billion, but institutional flows have rotated to Circle.

"USDC flipped USDT and took 70% of the volume," wrote @HodlDiplomat, a crypto markets commentator on X, citing a different methodology that strips out high-frequency activity to land on a smaller monthly total.

The catalyst is the US GENIUS Act, [signed into law in July 2025](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1582), which established full reserve, audit and compliance requirements for any dollar stablecoin marketed to American users. The law gave US banks and payment processors the legal cover to move flows to the only major stablecoin built for exactly that regime. Tether responded by launching a separate USAT token to attempt American compliance.

## Why It Matters For Visa, Mastercard And The Banks

Visa runs its own stablecoin settlement service. Select merchant acquirers can settle in USDC instead of through traditional banking hours. Mastercard joined Paxos's Global Dollar Network and now enables USDC, PYUSD, USDG and FIUSD across its network. Both card networks see the threat clearly enough to want a piece of it.

"Stablecoins settled $7.2 trillion onchain last month. ACH did $6 trillion. For the first time ever," wrote @BitcoinNews, the verified crypto news account, on April 15. The post called the moment "endgame for crypto."

Chainalysis, which sells enterprise blockchain analytics, projected this month in [a report that also markets its own tools](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/04/09/stablecoin-volumes-to-reach-usd719t-by-2035-as-generational-wealth-shift-speeds-up-crypto-adoption) that adjusted stablecoin volume could reach $719 trillion by 2035. Even with heavy discounting for the conflict, the trajectory puts onchain dollar settlement on a collision course with every legacy network at once.

The $7.5 trillion settlement number is the demand-side counterpart to a year of regulated infrastructure builds: the [GENIUS Act unlocking a $323 billion bank stablecoin market](https://www.forbes.com/sites/boazsobrado/2026/04/08/gamechanger-banks-suddenly-targeting-323-billion-stablecoin-market/), and [non-dollar stablecoins crossing $1.2 billion](https://www.forbes.com/sites/boazsobrado/2026/03/30/non-dollar-stablecoins-hit-12-billion-as-local-currencies-go-on-chain/) as local currencies move onchain.

## What's Real And What Isn't

The cautions are real.

Raw onchain volume includes DeFi liquidity provisioning, MEV and arbitrage flows that are not economic settlement. Artemis publishes both raw and adjusted figures. The $7.2-$7.5 trillion numbers above use the adjusted methodology. Analysts still disagree on the exact filter.

The sources are also conflicted. Circle, Stripe, Chainalysis and Artemis all sell tools that benefit from the narrative. The numbers are real, but the parties producing them have skin in the game.

The direction is harder to dispute. Stablecoin total supply has reached $315 billion, up from roughly $200 billion at the start of 2025. USDC's institutional flows show average transaction sizes consistent with B2B settlement and payroll. And the ACH crossover has now happened twice.

"The payment rails have shifted," OKX wrote.

For the banks and card networks that built ACH, the question for the second half of 2026 is no longer whether stablecoins are a real payment rail. It is whether they run their own corner of it, or watch Circle, Tether and the GENIUS-licensed bank issuers run it for them.

'Rails Have Shifted'—Stablecoins Topped ACH At $7.5 Trillion A Month

ByBoaz Sobrado,

Former Contributor.

Forbes contributors publish independent expert analyses and insights.
 Boaz Sobrado is a fintech leader and entrepreneur.
Apr 20, 2026, 09:15am EDT

"In February alone, stablecoin monthly volume hit $7.2 trillion, surpassing the US ACH network ($6.8T) for the first time in history," wrote Haonan Li, the co-founder and CEO of stablecoin payments firm Codex and a former Optimism core contributor.

The post landed in mid-April. American payments executives took a few weeks to notice.

The numbers come from Artemis Analytics. Stablecoin onchain settlement hit $7.2 trillion in February on a 30-day rolling basis. The US Automated Clearing House, the rail that has carried American payroll and B2B payments for half a century, settled $6.8 trillion in the same window. March brought $7.5 trillion in onchain stablecoin volume. The crossover is no longer a one-off.

OKX, the verified crypto exchange, put it bluntly two days after Haonan. "The payment rails have shifted. $7.2T in monthly stablecoin volume proves it," the exchange wrote on April 16.

For Visa, Mastercard and the US banks that built ACH, the comfortable story is over. Stablecoins are not a crypto-trader curiosity. They are a payment rail.

PROMOTED

USDC Has Quietly Overtaken USDT

The other shift inside the headline number is the dollar doing the work.

Circle's USDC processed roughly $2.2 trillion in adjusted year-to-date onchain volume. Tether's USDT did $1.3 trillion. The figures come from Mizuho Securities research shared in April. USDC now leads adjusted volume for the first time since 2019. Tether still dominates total market cap at around $184 billion versus USDC at $75-80 billion, but institutional flows have rotated to Circle.

"USDC flipped USDT and took 70% of the volume," wrote @HodlDiplomat, a crypto markets commentator on X, citing a different methodology that strips out high-frequency activity to land on a smaller monthly total.

The catalyst is the US GENIUS Act, signed into law in July 2025, which established full reserve, audit and compliance requirements for any dollar stablecoin marketed to American users. The law gave US banks and payment processors the legal cover to move flows to the only major stablecoin built for exactly that regime. Tether responded by launching a separate USAT token to attempt American compliance.

Why It Matters For Visa, Mastercard And The Banks

Visa runs its own stablecoin settlement service. Select merchant acquirers can settle in USDC instead of through traditional banking hours. Mastercard joined Paxos's Global Dollar Network and now enables USDC, PYUSD, USDG and FIUSD across its network. Both card networks see the threat clearly enough to want a piece of it.

"Stablecoins settled $7.2 trillion onchain last month. ACH did $6 trillion. For the first time ever," wrote @BitcoinNews, the verified crypto news account, on April 15. The post called the moment "endgame for crypto."

Chainalysis, which sells enterprise blockchain analytics, projected this month in a report that also markets its own tools that adjusted stablecoin volume could reach $719 trillion by 2035. Even with heavy discounting for the conflict, the trajectory puts onchain dollar settlement on a collision course with every legacy network at once.

The $7.5 trillion settlement number is the demand-side counterpart to a year of regulated infrastructure builds: the GENIUS Act unlocking a $323 billion bank stablecoin market, and non-dollar stablecoins crossing $1.2 billion as local currencies move onchain.

What's Real And What Isn't

The cautions are real.

Raw onchain volume includes DeFi liquidity provisioning, MEV and arbitrage flows that are not economic settlement. Artemis publishes both raw and adjusted figures. The $7.2-$7.5 trillion numbers above use the adjusted methodology. Analysts still disagree on the exact filter.

The sources are also conflicted. Circle, Stripe, Chainalysis and Artemis all sell tools that benefit from the narrative. The numbers are real, but the parties producing them have skin in the game.

The direction is harder to dispute. Stablecoin total supply has reached $315 billion, up from roughly $200 billion at the start of 2025. USDC's institutional flows show average transaction sizes consistent with B2B settlement and payroll. And the ACH crossover has now happened twice.

"The payment rails have shifted," OKX wrote.

For the banks and card networks that built ACH, the question for the second half of 2026 is no longer whether stablecoins are a real payment rail. It is whether they run their own corner of it, or watch Circle, Tether and the GENIUS-licensed bank issuers run it for them.
